question: Patient of 46 years of age, hypertensive and without other pathological antecedents of interest. He came to the consultation because he had presented a previous, non-painful left parasternal tumor of two months of evolution and without any other symptom. The physical examination shows a hard mass of 4.5 x 4 cm, not painful, without skin retraction and adhering to deep planes. Which of these statements is correct?

options.opa: Being a non-painful anterior mass, it should be considered a benign tumor.
options.opb: As a first step, a chondroid tumor should be ruled out since they are the most frequent in this location.
options.opc: It is not indicated to perform a biopsy because of the danger of local dissemination of the tumor.
options.opd: It is preferable to maintain a conservative attitude, evaluating the evolution and possible growth of the tumor.
